**Observations from the image:**

- **Affected plant part:** Banana fruits (fingers)
- **Visual features:**
  - Small, green banana fruits held in hand
  - Large, dark brown to black necrotic/rotting patches on the fruit surface (sides and body of the bananas, not confined to tips)
  - Lesions are irregular in shape and appear sunken/coalescing
  - Multiple fruits are affected
  - No leaf symptoms visible

**Reasoning through the classes:**

- **Anthracnose** — caused by *Colletotrichum musae*; classic symptom is dark brown/black sunken lesions on banana fruits, often large and irregular, appearing on the sides/body of the fruit. **Strongly matches.**
- **Cigar End Rot** — also affects fruit, but lesions are specifically confined to the distal tip (end) of the banana, giving a "cigar-like" dry black rot. The lesions here are on the body/sides, not the tip. **Does not match.**
- **Bunchy Top** — viral disease; affects the whole plant (bunched leaves, dark streaks in veins), not fruit in this way. **Does not match.**
- **Cordana Leaf Spot** — affects leaves, not fruit. **Does not match.**
- **Panama Disease** — Fusarium wilt; causes yellowing/wilting of leaves and internal pseudostem discoloration, not these fruit lesions. **Does not match.**
- **Yellow And Black Sigatoka** — affects leaves with yellow and black streaks/spots. **Does not match.**

The dark, irregular, coalescing necrotic patches on the sides of banana fruits are highly characteristic of **Anthracnose**.
